- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 73.08 → 74.89 in Example 1), then undercorrects later.
- Underestimates in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting mean reversion or lagged response to recent high prices.
- Forecasts tend to be smoother than true outcomes, missing volatility spikes and sharp reversals.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when history includes recent high prices (e.g., 72+ range).
- Horizon-specific: first 10 days show overestimation, last 10 days show underestimation — suggests asymmetric response to recent trends.
- Model fails to capture “rebound” after correction — e.g., after a dip, it doesn’t anticipate a quick recovery.
